newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's new prime minister names cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's new prime minister names cabinet.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand, who took office earlier this month, has announced a 34-member coalition cabinet, naming a confidant as finance minister, officials said on Tuesday.

There are 25 cabinet rank ministers including Chand and nine ministers of state, a royal palace statement said on Monday after Chand, once close to the palace, presented his nominations to King Birendra.

Chand, a traditional right-winger, named 22 cabinet ministers from the communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, widely seen as the backseat driver for his ruling Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP).
But most key portfolios, including finance and foreign affairs, remained with Chand's RPP. Two cabinet ministers were named from a junior constituent, the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP).
The finance ministry went to the RPP's Rabindra Nath Sharma, who was closely involved in toppling the previous Nepali Congress government and assembling Nepal's first left-right coalition.

A centre-right coalition headed by Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba of the centrist Nepali Congress quit office earlier this month after it lost a crucial parliamentary vote following a split in the RPP, which was its key partner.

RPP, which controls only 20 seats in the 205-member House of Representatives, the lower house of the Himalayan kingdom's parliament, provided 10 ministers including the prime minister in the cabinet named on Monday.

Chand announced last week that the new government would follow a "liberal economic policy based on national interest" but critics said the communists dominating the government may slow the pace of liberalisation.
The RPP's Prakash Chandra Lohani was named Foreign Minister. He held the same portfolio in the previous coalition.

The Nepali Congress won power in 1991 but its government fell due to revolt by party members forcing premature elections in 1994. The elections threw up a fragmented parliament, in which the UML controlled 90 seats.

The UML formed a minority government that fell in September 1995, when Deuba put together a centre-right coalition. This fell when Chand revolted with some of his supporters to topple the Nepali Congress-led government.
